items.title: The dependency-vetting check triggers on workflow action references
body: The security-hygiene.dependency-vetting deterministic trigger keys on package manifests only, so a diff adding googleapis/release-please-action@v5.0.0 — third-party code running with contents:write — showed 'not triggered' and the batch 11 T3 reviewer had to file the missing vetting record by hand.

Fix: extend the trigger — a diff that adds or changes a `uses:` reference under .github/workflows/ requires dependency_vetting with the workflow file in manifests and the action reference in dependencies. Requires the owner's ruling first: the check lives on a STANDING entry (both knowledge copies) and the runner change lives in crates/houserules/src/rules/audit.rs's `run_check` (batch 20 T3 retired template/tools/kb.mjs, the runner's pre-rewrite home).
Source: batch 11 branch review, violated_rules 2 and template_defects 2 (2026-09-03). Standing-entry change: OWNER RULING PENDING, listed in the batch 11 report.

items.title: Binary delivery channels for the rewritten kit (Tier 2)
body: RULED with HR-047: distribution targets the compiled binary, not npm-first. Deliverables: per-platform release binaries (linux and macOS on x64 and arm64, Windows) built and attached by CI at each release-please release, with checksums and a signing/notarization decision for macOS; mise via the ubi backend; an asdf plugin consuming the release binaries; a Homebrew tap; Scoop or winget; a curl-to-sh installer. npm RETIRES (RULED 2026-09-04, design.md 5.22): binary-only distribution; a wrapper package stays purely additive later if demand appears.

Prerequisite RULED 2026-09-04 (design.md 5.20): plain v<version>. include-component-in-tag goes false at the next config-touching task; the alias tag v0.2.0-alpha already points at the existing release commit, so every channel builds on the v* grammar from the first release.

External acts (the plugin repository, registry PRs, the tap) are owner-attended per the decision 3 precedent. Blocked by HR-047 producing the binary; the spec may land the tag-format ruling and the CI scaffolding earlier.
Source: owner, 2026-09-03 (Tier 2 direct, no Tier 0 or Tier 1 channels).

items.title: The README's pinned install tag follows each release
body: README.md pins the install form to houserules-v0.2.0-alpha in three places (the r0 unpinned form was the worse defect); nothing in the release flow updates them, so the next release leaves the README installing an old kit — a knowledge-base.state-only-the-source decay at the first post-merge release.

Fix: wire the pins into the release flow — release-please extra-files annotations if they support the shape, else one line in the restamp step of docs/runbook.md and the finishing-a-feature skill (update the README pins with the restamp commit). Decide the mechanism in the batch spec. Interlock: HR-048's tag-format ruling may rename the tag grammar these pins use — schedule together or after it.

Batch 19 T2: measured and wired. release-please v17.11.2's Generic updater treats a bare string in `extra-files` as annotation-scanned text, verified against its own source (src/updaters/generic.ts at the pinned tag) and the pinned config schema. Wired six pin lines in README.md (the shell-installer URL, the five direct-download archive links) via x-release-please-start-version/-end blocks placed outside the runnable code fences, plus the seeded template/.github/workflows/knowledge.yml's own install-step pin via one inline x-release-please-version marker -- seven lines total across the two files, each proven with a RED (pre-fix content, no markers, replacement count assert-fails) and GREEN (shipped content, exact count) reproduction of the updater's own regex logic. STAYS OPEN: the mechanism is wired, not yet verified live -- closes only once a real release-please release actually replaces these pins and a fresh capture confirms the new pin resolves (docs/specs/2026-09-06-batch-19-phase4.md §7's step two).
Source: batch 13 branch review, issue 2 (2026-09-03).

items.title: Modular installs: adopters choose the feature set
body: Owner intent recorded at the Tier-2 CLI-surface ruling (2026-09-04): houserules becomes modular — an adopter can install only backlog management, or rules management without the backlog, or the full kit. This is WHY the flat command surface keeps per-module checks (check-knowledge, check-backlog) and the Rust crate separates rules, backlog, and install modules.

Shape: a feature/selection mechanism in init (and update honoring it) that installs a subset of the payload — the seeded files, generated artifacts, skills, and checks scoped to the chosen modules; the stamp records the selection. Details to the batch spec when gated, AFTER the Tier-2 port completes (the port ships everything; the crate boundaries prepare the split).
Source: owner, 2026-09-04, at the batch 15 CLI-surface ruling; the Tier-2 spec's architecture section carries the boundary design.

items.title: Default starter rule set: docs and code-quality style adopters begin with
body: Owner intent (2026-09-04): adopters should start with a curated default set of rules — docs style and code-quality style in tag-pilot's vein — instead of a near-empty seed. Today template/knowledge/ ships 36 entries that are process-heavy (23 process entries) while quality carries 2 and writing-style 3; no docs-style or language-agnostic code-quality starter content exists.

Shape: curate a default entry set for the quality and writing-style topics (and a docs area if warranted), modeled on the tag-pilot checkout's rules as a READ-ONLY reference (houserules.tag-pilot-is-read-only). Content work, independent of the Tier-2 binary; interacts with HR-053 (a starter set is what a modular rules-only install would seed). Curation choices and any new areas go to the batch spec when gated.
Source: owner, 2026-09-04, mid batch 16.

items.title: Capture-file citations for oversized report evidence
body: Batch 16 branch review, template defect 1: task-4-report.json reached 583KB because all 41 tdd entries embed verbatim RED/GREEN inline; reviewers re-ran cycles anyway, and T5's fix round already invented the better shape (bulk evidence in named workspace files, byte-prefix-matching inline excerpts).

Change: let a tdd or live_run entry cite a workspace capture file by path for output beyond a stated size, keeping the first lines plus exit inline; standardize the t5-evidence/ convention in .claude/schemas/deliverables.json and both agent templates. Deferred from batch 16 because template changes trigger process.evals-rerun and the batch was already closing.
Source: batch 16 branch review retrospective, 2026-09-04.

items.title: kb audit: an explicit empty-range mode
body: Batch 16 branch review, template defect 2: T5's three empty-range audits (research task, no diff) produced three byte-identical near-vacuous files — every deterministic row passes trivially and none speaks to the actual deliverable; the schema still demands self_audit, so the ritual ran three times for no signal.

Change: give audit an explicit empty-range mode that says so in one summary row (it already emits empty_range: true), and let a research task's report point its evidence rows at the workspace doc instead of the diff. Ships in template/tools until the Tier-2 port owns audit (phase 2), then carries into the Rust audit.
Source: batch 16 branch review retrospective, 2026-09-04.

items.title: Seeded knowledge.yml needs an install step before it can run
body: Batch 18 T5 fix round 1 (task-5-review.json, findings "seeded CI gate + hook" and houserules.payload-runs-on-builtins): template/.github/workflows/knowledge.yml now runs houserules check-knowledge, houserules check-backlog, and houserules audit, but no step in that job puts the houserules binary on the runner -- an adopter's houserules init seeds a PR gate whose first real step fails. The dead actions/setup-node@v7 step is dropped in the same fix round; this item tracks the missing install step itself.

Batch 19 T2: the install step now exists. A pinned cargo-dist shell-installer step (`releases/download/v<version>/houserules-installer.sh`) runs before check-knowledge/check-backlog/audit, defended against jdx/mise-action (a new marketplace-action dependency plus an inline mise.toml an adopter repo does not otherwise carry) at batch 19 T2's commit "feat(template): install houserules before the seeded CI gate runs" and that task's report `implemented` field. No new dependency enters this repository's own manifests; dependency_vetting there is null.

STAYS OPEN: jblossey/houserules carries one release so far (houserules-v0.2.0-alpha, 2026-09-03), and it ships zero assets; the v0.2.0-alpha tag the install step's URL actually needs has no release of its own (the releases API confirms both facts, fix round 1 t2-evidence/releases-api-listing.json). Either way the pinned URL 404s. Fix round 1 also gave the step `shell: bash`, so that 404 aborts the step itself (GitHub's documented -o pipefail) instead of surfacing two steps later as a confusing 'houserules: command not found' -- but a real CI run of the seeded step still cannot succeed until HR-048's pipeline cuts a release with assets. Closes only then, once a live run of a freshly seeded repository's PR gate proves the install step end to end (docs/specs/2026-09-06-batch-19-phase4.md §7's step two) -- the wiring is done, the verification is not.

houserules.payload-runs-on-builtins (the invariant that the SessionStart hook and the CI gates run where nothing is installed) is amended at T6 to the ruled binary+POSIX contract, and again at T2 to name this step; both amendments land against the fact each carried at the time, not silently past it.
Source: batch 18 T5 fix round 1 review, filed by the implementer per process.no-tech-debt.

items.title: README's build-from-source step follows HR-048/HR-049's real channel
body: Batch 18 T6 fix round 1 (task-6-review.json, issue 2, knowledge-base.state-only-the-source): the README's runnable blocks called a bare `houserules` binary no install path supplied. The fix round's answer is a temporary "Building the houserules binary" section (`git clone` this repository, `cargo install --path crates/houserules --bin houserules`) placed before the first bare `houserules` call, explicitly marked pending HR-048.

This item tracks retiring that section once HR-048 ships a real binary delivery channel: replace the build-from-source block with the shipped install form (the release-asset download, mise/ubi, or whichever channel HR-048 lands), and re-verify every runnable block top to bottom against it. Interlocked with HR-049 (the README's pinned install tag following each release) -- both touch the same blocks and should land together or in HR-049's wake, the same ordering HR-063 already notes for the seeded CI workflow's install step.
Blocked on HR-048; cannot land before it.

Batch 19 T2's commit "docs(readme): flip install and quick start to the real binary channels" performed the retirement: the build-from-source section is gone and the install blocks ship the real channels with dated PENDING control runs proving each fails for the right reason today (no release with assets). STAYS OPEN until step two: docs/runbook.md step 6's README install-block re-walk at the first release with assets closes it.
Source: batch 18 T6 fix round 1 review, issue 2 (2026-09-06).

items.title: release-please's tag push needs a token that starts release.yml
body: Batch 19 task 1 review, important finding: `.github/workflows/release-please.yml` invokes `googleapis/release-please-action@v5.0.0` with no `token:` input, so it tags and releases on the default `GITHUB_TOKEN`. GitHub suppresses workflow runs for events that token creates, so the tag it pushes will not start cargo-dist's generated `.github/workflows/release.yml` (houserules.default-token-tags-start-no-workflows records the mechanism). The pipeline would cut a tag and a draft release and upload zero artifacts, silently.

Two documented fixes, either closes the gap: (a) pass a PAT or GitHub App installation token as `release-please-action`'s `token:` input, so the tag push carries a real identity; (b) add a `github-script` step to release-please.yml, gated on the action's `release_created` output, that calls `workflow_dispatch` on release.yml directly, needing no PAT.

OWNER-ATTENDED: the choice is a secrets-management and workflow-ownership decision, not a technical unknown. Blocks the first real release-please release from actually publishing binaries; HR-049 and HR-063's live re-verification (spec 7's step two) wait on it. T2's runbook release section must name HR-068 so the owner meets the decision where the release is performed.
Source: batch 19 task 1 review, issue 3 (2026-09-06).

items.title: Flip pr-run-mode back to plan once a real release proves the pipeline
body: Batch 19 task 1 re-review r2, new_breakage: dist-workspace.toml's pr-run-mode = "upload" carries a written exit criterion in its own comment (flips to "plan" at the first config-touching task after the first real release proves the pipeline end to end) but no backlog item schedules that task, so nothing queues the revert.
Trigger: the first real release-please release runs the generated release pipeline end to end (host/create/announce succeed, artifacts publish) -- the proof step one could not perform.
Act: set pr-run-mode = "plan" in dist-workspace.toml, re-run `dist generate`, and remove the swatinem/rust-cache@v2 step it drags in (dependency_vetting can drop that entry in the same task).

Interlock: blocked by HR-068 (the token gap must resolve before a release-please tag can start release.yml at all) and rides HR-048's own pipeline slice; the dist-workspace.toml comment beside pr-run-mode cites this id.
Source: batch 19 task 1 review, fix round 2, new_breakage issue 2 (2026-09-07).

items.title: mise's ubi backend is deprecated; README's install form needs a migration plan
body: Batch 19 task 2, README channel walk: `mise use ubi:jblossey/houserules` (the ruled form, docs/specs/2026-09-06-batch-19-phase4.md §4) still resolves and installs, but mise's own current docs (docs/dev-tools/backends/ubi.md, checked 2026-09-07) mark the `ubi` backend deprecated in favor of `github:owner/repo`, and a live control run on this machine (mise 2026.7.18) prints `This will be removed in mise 2027.1.0`.

The `github:` backend covers the same case (a correctly named GitHub release asset, no registry act) with a stated migration path: replace `ubi:owner/repo` with `github:owner/repo`; the `matching`/`matching_regex` options carry over unchanged. Nothing in this batch's own release pipeline depends on ubi specifically -- the archive-naming work (T1) targets ubi's OS/arch/libc matching, which the github backend's own docs describe as equivalent pre-filtering, not identical, so the switch needs its own verification pass, not a blind rename.

OWNER-ATTENDED: swapping the documented channel is a support-surface decision (which backend adopters are told to use), not a technical unknown. Gate: the README's mise block cannot be walked against a real asset until HR-048's pipeline cuts a release, so this decision rides the SAME first-release re-verification step docs/runbook.md's step 6 names for HR-063/HR-049 -- walk `mise use ubi:jblossey/houserules` for real at that moment, decide whether to swap to `mise use github:jblossey/houserules` in the same act (both need a real release to verify, so splitting them into two acts only doubles the owner's trips to this decision), and keep the `ubi:` form's fresh-install control-run evidence for the before/after comparison. mise 2027.1.0's removal date stays the outer bound: if the first release lands well before then, the swap can still wait for a later, unhurried pass; if 2027.1.0 approaches with no release yet, act on the deprecation alone, ubi-only, without a real asset to test against.
Source: batch 19 task 2, README channel walk (2026-09-07).

items.title: Narrow check-report-claims' paste-run lint: quote-aware placeholder, $(...)-aware tokenizer
body: Batch 20 T2 fix round 1 review, important findings 3-4: the paste-run lint (HR-071) ships with two measured false-positive vehicles, both disclosed as Limits bullets in crates/houserules/src/report_claims.rs rather than narrowed. (1) The appended-annotation check's subshell exemption only covers a `(...)` wrapping the WHOLE command; a chained `cmd1 && (cmd2)` reads as an appended annotation instead — .superpowers/sdd/2026-09-04-batch-17/task-2-report.json live_run[8] is a real instance the shipped checker flags. (2) The placeholder check ignores quote_mask's state entirely, so a quoted angle-bracket literal that is command DATA (an HTML-comment probe, or a `Co-Authored-By: ... <email>` trailer this repository's own standing no-coauthor rule guarantees will keep generating) misreads as a placeholder — the lint's most frequent false positive at filing time: 5 instances across 4 workspace reports.

The narrowing: (a) a quote-aware placeholder arm in find_placeholder, skipping any span quote_mask already marks as inside a quoted string; (b) a $(...)-aware tokenizer arm in quote_mask, tracking that a same-character quote re-opened inside a `$(...)`/`` `...` `` command substitution starts a fresh, independent quoted region rather than closing the one around the whole substitution (the vehicle report_claims.rs's own Limits section discloses from batch 20 T2's first pass, 2 instances in that same review's own corpus sweep). Deferred per process.no-tech-debt: both are bounded, well-scoped engineering — quote_mask already carries the byte-level state the placeholder check would need to consult, and the $(...) arm needs a small quote-context stack, not a rewrite — not a correctness blocker for HR-071's shipped form, which already discloses both gaps with their measured instances rather than shipping them silently.

items.title: implementer template: edit reports via temp file, validate, then move
body: From the batch 20 branch review: a jq quoting slip in T4's fix round briefly overwrote the report with an empty file; recovery depended on an intact intermediate copy. The implementer template gains one sentence: edit a report by writing to a temp file, running houserules validate on it, then moving it over the original - never in-place through a pipeline whose failure truncates the target. Template edit: rides the next template-touching batch and pays the evals co-change there.
Source: batch 20 branch review, template_defects[1].

items.title: Seeded escape hatch names its upstream destination
body: RULED 2026-09-08 (design.md 5.51): the implementer template's closing-act false-positive branch gains the destination - report the vehicle upstream (an issue at github.com/jblossey/houserules). Template edit: rides the next template-touching batch alongside HR-078 and pays the evals co-change there.

items.title: release-please misses commits that change the embedded template/ payload but not crates/houserules/**
body: HR-073's release-type: rust at crates/houserules moved release-please's commit attribution off the repository root: CommitSplit.split (commit-split.ts:99) now counts a commit toward the crate's next version only when it touches crates/houserules/**, since the ROOT_PROJECT_PATH special case that used to assign every commit (manifest.ts:700-701) no longer applies. crates/houserules/src/install.rs:232-234 embeds `../../template/` into the shipped binary via #[derive(RustEmbed)], so a commit that changes only template/ (or README.md, or another root-level path) changes shipped code and, under the new attribution, opens no release PR at all.

Measured over v0.2.0-alpha..6aa19e0 (batch 20 T5 fix round 1 review): 82 of 119 commits touch no path under crates/houserules/, and 7 of 27 feat/fix commits are unattributed under the new package path -- four of them (7460c77b feat(template), 6ac1aaa7 fix(template), 719d3f58 fix(tools), 101555ef fix(template)) change the embedded payload directly, per t5-evidence/hr081-template-payload-commits.sh's own enumeration by touched path rather than commit subject (fix round 2: a subject-scoped read of the same range missed 719d3f58, 'fix(tools): validate rejects incomplete terminal reports', which touches no crates/houserules/ path and two template/ files). Today enough crate-side commits ride along that a release PR still opens; a cycle whose only changes are template/, README.md, or the knowledge base would silently ship nothing.

The package path is not the thing to change: release-type rust at '.' (the root) would take the Rust strategy's workspace branch and push a CargoToml update for the root manifest, which cargo-toml.ts:37-40 throws on ('is not a package manifest') since the root Cargo.toml carries no [package] section under this workspace's virtual-manifest shape -- reviewer-confirmed and re-verified by the implementer. The gap needs a different remedy, not a reversal of HR-073's ruling.

Candidate remedies (this item carries the question, not the answer): (a) an extra-files or component-mapping addition to release-please-config.json that attributes template/** changes to the crate's own path for commit-attribution purposes; (b) a documented pre-release rule that a payload-changing commit always rides alongside a crate-side commit before a release is cut, checked by hand or by a gate. Owner picks.
Source: batch 20 T5 fix round 1 review (task-5-review.json), important finding 1.

items.title: Cargo.lock's houserules version line goes stale after a release-please merge, no owner yet
body: HR-073's release-type: rust config gives Cargo.lock no extra-files entry: the Rust strategy's own built-in Cargo.lock update (rust.ts:124-128) targets addPath('Cargo.lock') under the package's own path -- crates/houserules/Cargo.lock, which does not exist, since this repository's real Cargo.lock sits at the workspace root -- so the update silently no-ops (github.ts:850-861) and a release-please merge bumps crates/houserules/Cargo.toml's version without touching Cargo.lock's own recorded entry for the same package.

Verified live (batch 20 T5, and re-verified in fix round 1 with a bounded, rerunnable sweep, t5-evidence/ci-lock-flag-sweep.sh): no --locked/--frozen/--offline flag exists anywhere in this repository's own CI surface (.github/, mise.toml, dist-workspace.toml) or in cargo-dist v0.32.0's own build path (cargo-dist/src/build/{cargo,mod,fake,generic}.rs), so any subsequent cargo build/check/test invocation -- including the one dist build runs when cutting a release -- silently rewrites the stale line to match Cargo.toml, with no failure anywhere today.

The risk: a --locked consumer would fail outright. Reproduced live (bumping the crate's version in this checkout, running the command, then reverting): `cargo check --locked` fails with 'cannot update the lock file ... because --locked was passed' (t5-evidence/cargo-check-locked-fails.log). Nothing in this repository's pipeline runs with --locked today, so this is a latent risk, not an active break -- but it has no tracked owner now that HR-073 is ticked done, and process.no-tech-debt wants an accepted gap carried by a backlog item, not by a closed one's body.

Candidate remedies (open): extend the post-release-please-merge restamp procedure (docs/runbook.md) to also run a Cargo.lock refresh (e.g. `cargo update -p houserules --precise <version>` or a plain `cargo check`) and commit it alongside the kit-version restamp; or accept the residue indefinitely with this item standing as its documented risk record. Filed separately from HR-081 (same review round, same closed item, different mechanism -- a stale lockfile line versus a missed release PR -- so a remedy for one does not gate the other).
Source: batch 20 T5 fix round 1 review (task-5-review.json), minor finding 3.

items.title: check-backlog gains a --fix arm for a non-round-tripping backlog file
body: Filed by the task-1 fix round 1 review (minor issue 8): check-backlog's round-trip finding (HR-076) names a concrete remedy per file class, but only backlog/items/*.json has a shipped command that can reach it (`houserules set`). The other five files (schema.json, amendments.json, batches.json, decisions.json, parked.json) have no writer at all, so an adopter who trips this on one of them is told to hand-reproduce serde_json's pretty-printer byte for byte.

Candidate: a `--fix` arm on check-backlog (or a small subcommand) that rewrites the named file through the same `crate::emit::emit` call the check already compares against, so the repair path and the check path stay the same function. Not built in the fix round that filed it: the message-only remedy was the scoped fix; a --fix arm is a larger surface (does it fix every diverging file in one run, or one named file? does it need a --dry-run?) that deserves its own task.

items.title: teach --sanctioned in the three dispatch agent templates and the orchestrating skill
body: Corrected at batch-21 T2 fix round 1 (review critical issue 2): round 0 asserted this item's own home list by hand rather than from a real enumeration, and the assertion was wrong twice over. The retained, rerunnable sweep (t2-evidence/sweep-audit-invocation-sentences.sh, a git ls-files walk grepping four audit-invocation forms; t2-evidence/sweep-audit-invocation-dispositions.md dispositions all 43 hits) found one home round 0 missed entirely: crates/houserules/src/rules/render.rs:47, the PROTOCOL constant that renders the audit invocation into .claude/skills/project-knowledge/SKILL.md and every adopter's generated skill. That file is tracked and NOT a template file, so it needed no deferral -- it was fixed in the same fix round (ruling R3): PROTOCOL[2] gained one clause teaching --sanctioned, and houserules render plus gen-goldens regenerated every downstream copy (root and mini SKILL.md, both render goldens).

Corrected again at fix round 2 (re-review critical issue 2): round 1 read the sweep's own silence on template/.claude/skills/orchestrating/SKILL.md as proof the file teaches no audit invocation. That is a claim about the sweep's four patterns, not about the file: `grep -n -i audit` on it returns 8 lines, and three of them teach the invocation's own flags (--ids, --workspace in place of --report) in prose forms none of the sweep's patterns match -- 'the audit command's `--ids <the Knowledge ids>`', 'its audit runs `--workspace <WORKSPACE>` in place of `--report`', and 'A branch review's audit runs `--workspace <WORKSPACE>`' (lines 39, 44, and 53 at this revision; batch 23 T2 shifts them to 41, 46, and 55, a line-pin drift that revision, not number, now names). The sweep script's own header and the dispositions file now name this pattern-recall gap.

What remains genuinely deferred, per the corrected sweep: three template files teaching a human or agent the audit invocation syntax to copy verbatim -- template/.claude/agents/implementer.md, template/.claude/agents/task-reviewer.md, and template/.claude/agents/branch-reviewer.md (their root .claude/agents/*.md mirrors are KIT_OWNED consequences of editing the template, not separate homes) -- plus template/.claude/skills/orchestrating/SKILL.md, teaching the invocation's flags without a form the sweep's patterns can see. Every existing sentence in all four stays correct as written -- --sanctioned is additive, so nothing is stale -- but each could additionally name --sanctioned as the mechanism for a spec-booked interim fail, replacing the hand-narration pattern that cost batch 20 fourteen audits and review rounds (HR-077's own incident). Every one of the four is a template file, off-limits under batch 21's task-2 brief (shared constraints: "NO template/agent/eval edits") regardless of any other trigger; editing implementer.md or task-reviewer.md specifically also co-changes process.evals-rerun's own check (its trigger names only those two plus .claude/evals/*.json, not branch-reviewer.md or the orchestrating skill), so either also owes the shared evals rerun.

Filed rather than edited in-branch, per that constraint. Fold into a future template-touching batch's plan (the same batch that lands HR-078/HR-080, per the batch-21 spec's own NOT-in-scope list) alongside its shared evals rerun; that plan should also widen the sweep's pattern set so a flag-only teaching form like the orchestrating skill's own is not invisible to it again.

Ruled out of scope at batch 23 T2 review (docs/specs/2026-09-12-batch-23-template-cluster.md §2 amendment): template/.claude/skills/orchestrating/SKILL.md contains no `houserules audit` invocation to copy verbatim, only flag prose -- teaching --sanctioned there has no invocation to attach it to. The three agent templates (implementer.md, task-reviewer.md, branch-reviewer.md) are the complete home set this item delivers; all three gained --sanctioned at batch 23 T2.

items.title: Template-batch trio: tree-binary rule, resume narrative rewrite, subject-derived sweeps
body: From the batch 21 branch review's template_defects, all three homes are template files and ride the next template-touching batch (with HR-078, HR-080, HR-090; one shared evals rerun where triggered).

(1) Orchestrating skill / retrieval protocol: when the current branch changes generated output, run all gates through the tree binary (cargo run --release --bin houserules) and re-install after merge - the stale installed binary false-failed check-knowledge all batch and cost a standing ledger workaround.

(2) Implementer template, resume path: on resume after an interruption, and at the end of every fix round, rewrite implemented/self_review/concerns from the tree at HEAD; a carried sentence is unverified - batch 21 T2's resumed round carried five stale statements and cost a full review round.

(3) Task-reviewer template, closure-claim check: derive the enumeration's pattern from the claim's SUBJECT via a spelling-discovery probe over the corpus; reject a closure keyed to one artifact's name - three sweeps this batch were bounded narrower than their claims.

items.title: Limits sentence: cite-into-artifact is the ephemeral-narrative pattern
body: RULED 2026-09-11 (design.md 5.57): one sentence in report_claims.rs's HR-075 Limits section records the standing answer - a narrative names an ephemeral path's class and cites the literal in a retained workspace capture; no checker escape. Rides the next implementation branch.

items.title: Restate the nine unreachable historical SHA markers to event locators
body: RULED 2026-09-11 (batch 21 report, 'Fix both'): the nine pre-batch-21 'verified live at commit X' markers whose SHAs no clone can resolve restate to durable event locators per knowledge-base.cite-durable-refs. The enumeration is retained at the batch-21 workspace's branch-fix-evidence/sweep-unreachable-shas.sh (12 rows; the two in-scope fixed at batch 21; these nine are the remainder). items.title: Public-surface sweep: no private paths, emails, or attribution anywhere public
body: Owner ruling 2026-09-11 after a sweep of every PR (all states), comment, review, issue, release, commit message on every remote branch, and tracked file on main. Cleaned the same day: session links and tool-attribution lines in the descriptions of PRs #3, #4, #5, #9, #12; a git+file URL under the maintainer's home directory in docs/plans/2026-09-01-batch-2.md; the batch-14 fixture reports and validate_stats_audit_parity.rs now carry a /home/maintainer/... prefix (houserules.corpus-batch14-fixtures-are-committed updated); the standing rule houserules.tag-pilot-is-read-only, one backlog body, two plan/spec documents, and the fixture review evidence name the tag-pilot checkout without a path.

Done 2026-09-11: the owner ran docs/history/2026-09-11-author-email-rewrite.sh (filter-branch over every ref, 292 commits, 0 left with the personal address, force-pushed under a temporarily disabled ruleset, the old-to-new map beside it). The same day FROZEN_SHA moved to that rewrite commit and gen-goldens regenerated the read-parity and render goldens, which had kept the old tag-pilot path from the earlier pin's tree. Every sha cited before this date resolves through the map.

Record of an id collision: this item was first filed as HR-093 on the hygiene branch while batch 21 filed its own HR-093 (diff-shape-gate retirement); the batch-21 close kept its item and dropped this one, and a later edit meant for this item landed in that HR-093's third paragraph until the token change restored it from the pre-edit tree. Re-filed here under a fresh id.

items.title: Main needs the code owner's approval for everyone but the owner; Dependabot auto-merge runs on the owner's token
body: Owner ruling 2026-09-11: only the owner merges to main without an approval; every other contributor's PR needs the owner's approving review. Applied as a second ruleset `approval` on the default branch (one approving review, code-owner review required, stale reviews dismissed on push, threads resolved) whose only bypass actor is the repository admin role. The first ruleset `main` (the eight required checks incl. CodeQL, linear history, no force-push, PR required) keeps no bypass and binds the owner too. GitHub cannot exempt one rule inside a ruleset, hence the split.

Consequence and the ruled fix: GitHub refuses the Actions app as a bypass actor on a user-owned repository, so a merge enabled with GITHUB_TOKEN now waits for an approval and the HR-092 auto-merge stalls. The owner chose the token route: .github/workflows/dependabot-auto-merge.yml enables auto-merge with a fine-grained personal access token of the owner (Contents and Pull requests read/write on this repository only), stored as the Dependabot secret DEPENDABOT_AUTOMERGE_TOKEN (a Dependabot-triggered workflow reads that store, not Actions secrets). A merge performed as the owner also starts the push workflows on main, which lifts HR-092's GITHUB_TOKEN limit for these merges.

PENDING proof: the next minor or patch Dependabot PR merging on its own with the workflow green. Flip to done with that PR's number. HR-068 (a token for the release flow) stays a separate ruling: release-please edits a workflow file, which needs the `workflows` permission this token does not carry.

items.title: `get` only resolves HR-/A-/PP- ids; a project's own --id-prefix is not respected
body: `is_backlog_id` (crates/houserules/src/get.rs) hardcodes the HR-/A-/PP- id shapes rather than reading the project's own stamped id prefix (`.houserules.json`'s `idPrefix`, default `WI`). Reproduced live at batch 22 T1: `houserules init --dir <scratch>` with no `--id-prefix` seeds `WI-nnn` items, and `houserules get WI-001` then fails with `unknown id "WI-001"` even though the item exists and `list`/`batch` both resolve it fine.
Found incidentally while live-running HR-105's archive sweep (docs/plans/2026-09-11-batch-22-stewardship.md, T1); out of that task's own scope, so filed here rather than fixed in place.

Consequence recorded at batch 22 T1 fix round 1 (task-1-review.json, issue 3): this gap is not only latent. houserules archive makes it active -- a WI-prefixed item's archived record becomes unreachable by get in ANY project once swept, not merely unreached before the sweep the way it was before HR-105. get's own archive fallback works around the consequence by trying both archive lookups regardless of routing (fix round 1); this item still tracks the underlying matcher fix.

items.title: find-shell-tool-refs.rs carries two exception entries that now match nothing
body: `exceptions()` in crates/houserules/src/bin/find-shell-tool-refs.rs names two exceptions -- `template/tools/kb.mjs` and `crates/houserules/src/rules/read.rs` -- that a live run (`cargo run --bin find-shell-tool-refs`) shows currently matching zero hits: kb.mjs no longer exists in the tree, and read.rs's own sole `kb.sh`-naming line was removed by the batch 22 T3a comment sweep. Only the `install.rs` exception still fires (4 hits).

Found while sweeping this file's comments at batch 22 T3b: correcting a stale doc claim about read.rs's hit count surfaced that the underlying exception entry is now dead weight, not only the sentence describing it.

Removing the two dead `Exception` entries (and `RUST_FILES`'s `rules/read.rs` member, if nothing else in that file still needs the scan) is a code change, out of scope for a comment-only sweep; filed here rather than fixed in place.

The surviving `install.rs` exception's own `reason` string literal narrates its own history (batch/phase/fix-round references) the same way the two removed entries' reasons did. It is user-facing output, not a comment, so the comment-only sweep correctly left it alone -- but once the two dead entries are deleted, rewrite this one's `reason` to the present-tense rule it states (RETIRED's own doc/test are FILE PATHS the deletion mechanism removes, narrowed to exactly that window so a whole-file exception cannot swallow an unrelated hit) in the same commit.

items.title: .gitattributes carries the same history narration HR-106's keep/drop line prunes from code
body: HR-106's keep/drop line (docs/specs/2026-09-11-batch-22-stewardship.md §3) drops batch/task/round references, commit SHAs, and CI run/job ids from comments, keeping only the current constraint. The repository root's own .gitattributes carries exactly that class of history narration in its four comment blocks, confirmed present at HEAD: PR #6 and CI run 34056471594 (the tests/goldens/** block), commit e36c4b2 (the tests/fixtures/** block, alongside batch 20 T3 and HR-084), commits 0bb27a0 and 2174a9f (the .claude/rules/**/.claude/skills/project-knowledge/** block, alongside batch 20 T6), and HR-054 (the tests/corpus/** block).

Found during HR-106's own T3c comment sweep of crates/houserules/tests/**; .gitattributes is not a code file under any of spec §3's three file lists (crates/houserules/src/**, crates/houserules/tests/**, tools/*.sh, .githooks/*, and the template shell copies), so the sweep left it untouched, per scope.

Prune each block to the current constraint it states (which paths get -text, and why -text specifically, not the discovery history), the same rewrite HR-106's own sweeps already applied across crates/houserules/src/** and crates/houserules/tests/**.

items.title: Template-cluster riders from the batch-22 branch review
body: Filed at batch-22 close from the branch review's retrospective (branch-review.json, template_defects) and the branch-fix-1 review. Rides the template cluster (HR-078/080/090/094/095/096) for its shared evals rerun; the agent-template edits below trigger process.evals-rerun.

1. Declare the deliverable task-id shape once and derive all three filename patterns from it, with a parity test. Today the schema accepts lettered ids, audit/review discovery matches task-.+, and reports matched task-\\d+ until the batch-22 branch fix widened it; three answers to one question.

2. branch-reviewer template, audit step: after the workspace audit, compare the report count the audit's evidence names against the workspace's task-*-report.json listing; a mismatch invalidates every report-field row.

3. implementer template, report step: write implemented/self_review sentences from the tree at the final HEAD, re-running each measurement; a sentence carried from a draft, a review, or a dispatch is re-derived before it ships. This instruction closed batch 22's five-task report-drift arc as dispatch prose and belongs in the template.

4. implementer template, knowledge_used: the rules a task exists to enforce count as relied-on; list them. All three batch-22 sweep reports omitted writing-style.code-comments/doc-comments and degraded the stats signal.
5. orchestrating skill, batch close checklist: every task-*-report.json in the workspace has a ledger row stating its close commit and round count before the branch review dispatches.

items.title: update restamps an entry whose content equals the current payload
body: Found at the batch-22 close-out update run: an entry edited to the exact content the current payload ships (both copies edited together, the dogfood norm) classifies Modified against its stale baseline and prints 'kept (locally modified)' on every update forever, because only at-baseline entries restamp.

Refinement: when current content equals the current payload content, restamp silently - the adopter holds exactly what the kit ships, so there is nothing to keep or report. Applies to KIT_OWNED files and knowledge entries alike.
Seven such lines print on this repository's own update today; the report noise grows with every ruled wording change.

items.title: Deterministic citation-line check in check-report-claims
body: RULED 2026-09-12 (batch 22 report, standing proposal 1): extend the report-claims gate deterministically - every path:NNN (and path:NNN-MMM) citation in a report's narrative fields must name an existing file, and NNN must not exceed that file's line count at HEAD. Catches the stream-index-as-file-line class (batch 22 T3c: 13 of 33 catalogue citations) and dangling pins mechanically, where judged review rounds catch them today.
Design note: command fields stay exempt (the ephemeral-path precedent); the check reads the tracked tree and the batch workspace the report cites.

items.title: The schema engine silently ignores unsupported keywords - a gate that narrows itself
body: Found at batch 23 T1 review round 2, proven empirically: rules/check.rs's validate handles only $ref, enum, type, pattern, minLength, maxLength, minimum, items, uniqueItems, required, properties, and additionalProperties; any other keyword (oneOf, anyOf, allOf, const, maximum, format) falls through every branch and the field goes UNCHECKED with no finding printed. A scratch schema whose taskNumber carried oneOf stopped raising the 'must be integer or string' error entirely.

This is the class quality.gates-derive-their-scope exists for: a validation gate that narrows itself in silence. It is also what made a review-suggested oneOf fix unimplementable at T1 (the two-descriptions fallback shipped instead).

Remedy, pick one at spec time: the engine reports an unsupported keyword as a named finding (the way an uncompilable pattern already is - houserules.crash-paths-are-named's shape), or it grows real combinator support. The named-finding route is the smaller, safer first step and unblocks combinators later.
